name: Virginia
scope: Presumptive formula only for pendente lite (temporary) spousal support: § 16.1-278.17:1 (juvenile and domestic relations district courts) and § 20-103 (circuit courts). Final spousal support under § 20-107.1 is factor-based with no formula.

formula.text: With minor children in common: 26% of the payor spouse's monthly gross income minus 58% of the payee spouse's monthly gross income. With no minor children in common: 27% of the payor's monthly gross income minus 50% of the payee's. Gross income as defined in § 20-108.2. Spousal support is determined before child support. Applies only when combined monthly gross income does not exceed $10,000; deviation for good cause.

duration.text: No formula for duration. § 20-107.1(C): support may be for a defined duration, an undefined duration, a lump sum, or a combination. § 20-107.1(D): when the right to future support is reserved, a rebuttable presumption that the reservation lasts 50% of the time between the date of marriage and the date of separation.

eligibility.text: § 20-107.1(B): no permanent support to a spouse against whom adultery (§ 20-91(A)(1)) is established, unless denial would be a manifest injustice shown by clear and convincing evidence. § 20-107.1(E) lists 13 factors for nature, amount and duration.

taxNote.text: Federal: for divorce or separation agreements executed after 2018 (or older ones modified to adopt the new rule), the payer cannot deduct alimony and the recipient does not include it in gross income (IRS Topic No. 452).

facts.text: The pendente lite formula is presumptive only where the spouses' combined monthly gross income is $10,000 or less (§ 16.1-278.17:1(E); § 20-103(I)).
A pendente lite order has no presumptive effect on the final decision in the case (§ 20-103(J)).
A reservation of the right to future spousal support is presumed to last half the time from marriage to separation, and that duration cannot be modified (§ 20-107.1(D)).
Adultery bars permanent support unless denial would be a manifest injustice (§ 20-107.1(B)).

uncertain: The brief's figures (28%/58% with children; 30%/50% without) are outdated: the current text (2020, c. 651) reads 26%/58% and 27%/50%.
